summary.headline: Suprajit H1 FY27 consolidated revenue up 22% to INR2,205 crore and EBITDA up 40% to INR267 crore; H1 margin 12.1%.
summary.overview: Consolidated H1 FY27 revenue rose 22% to INR2,205 crore and operating EBITDA rose 40% to INR267 crore, with Q2 EBITDA margin at 12.2%. Management said Q2 showed margin recovery at ICM and PLE after Q1 pricing pressure, and GCM margin rose from 7.4% to 10%+ as restructuring completed. Standalone H1 revenue grew 18% to INR1,034 crore while standalone EBITDA grew only 3% to INR149 crore. Management guided H2 consolidated margin slightly above H1, conditional on commodity prices and the Middle East conflict, while SED margins remain under pressure from component cost inflation and pricing negotiations.

financial_highlights.change: Q2 EBITDA grew about 27% YoY per Chairman

financial_highlights.metric: ICM India cable and mechatronics revenue (Q2)
financial_highlights.change: Margin up from 12.8% in Q1; OEM and beyond-cable growth about 20%

financial_highlights.value: Growth close to 15%; EBITDA growth 30%; margin 14.4%

financial_highlights.change: Electronics margin below double digits in Q2
vs about INR350 crore last year; mainly forex-driven
vs FY27 guidance of 27%-28%; attributed to deferred tax

segments.name: GCM (Global Cables and Mechatronics, incl. SCS)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 24% and EBITDA 69% with margin up from 7.4% to 10%+; H1 EBITDA more than doubled. Guidance of 10%-12% margin is intact; Q1 dip attributed to mix, seasonality and expedited freight.

segments.name: ICM (India Cable and Mechatronics)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew close to 14% in Q2, with OEM and beyond-cable up about 20% and aftermarket (incl. OE spares) in single digits. Margin recovered to 15.3% from 12.8% in Q1.

segments.name: PLE (Phoenix Lighting and Electricals)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew close to 15% and EBITDA 30% with margin at 14.4% vs 6.7% in Q1; management said 14.4% is not sustainable alone and Q1 and Q2 should be read together. Trifa remains soft; ramp-up with largest US retailer ongoing.

segments.name: SED (Sensors, Electronics and Displays)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 50.4% YoY led by digital clusters and electronic throttle controls, with margin under pressure from component cost inflation and logistics. Management expects margins to return to double digits once new pricing is agreed; capacity expansion underway.

segments.name: STC (Suprajit Technology Centre)
segments.commentary: New STC building due for completion this quarter. CBS brake production ramping; first drum brake system going into production for an EV two-wheeler in Bengaluru and first export parking brake supply started. Hydraulic brake system under testing, with positive news expected next year.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated FY27 EBITDA margin guidance 12%-13.5%; H2 margin expected slightly better than H1 in percentage terms, subject to commodities and Middle East conflict.
GCM margin guidance 10%-12% reaffirmed; management aspires to move toward the upper end.
ICM, PLE and SED guided to comfortable double-digit margins for FY27, broadly in line with prior year; PLE full-year margin expected similar to last year.
GCM H2 growth may be below the H1 rate of 22%-24% but still strong double-digit based on customer commitments.

FY27 capex about INR200 crore, roughly half spent by mid-November; future capex around 3%-4% of revenue (about INR200 crore annualised). Payout guidance 30%-40%; the balance goes to capex and debt reduction.
SED growth of 50% is seen as ambitious for sustaining; strong growth expected into FY28.
capex_capacity: Capex around INR200 crore for FY27, about half incurred by mid-November 2026.
SAL (Suprajit Automotive Private Limited, export wing) setting up a greenfield cable plant in Chennai.
SED: construction started on a much larger facility in the vacated part of the existing plant after moving to a rented facility.
STC new building to be completed in Q3 FY27; largest consolidated CWIP (about INR50 crore) mainly relates to STC completion.
China operations: about 25 million (currency unspecified) annual revenue from two plants; 8-9 of about 20-22 awarded EV OEM projects in commercial production, with 10-12 more over the next year.
Consolidation of European warehouses remains on track.
demand_pricing: Europe weak, Germany particularly; customer volumes on some awarded programmes reduced (e.g. 500,000 sets to 300,000-400,000), but management says European business still grows on new wins.
US: growth from replacing competitors' contracts; US underlying market growing only 1-2%.
China: growth driven by the largest EV maker ramping offtake.
Indian auto industry grew 20%+ on lower GST, but H2 faces a higher base effect.
SED wins broad-based across OEMs, products and geographies; commodity and electronic component inflation with pricing renegotiation taking longer than expected.
ICM pricing reviewed with customers once or twice a year; electronics pricing discussions being held more frequently.
Aftermarket in single digits as OEM demand strengthens, because owners defer servicing.

qa_highlights.question: How will cash flows be split between capex, payouts and debt reduction over two years?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex about INR200 crore; ongoing capex about 3%-4% of revenue. Payouts guided at 30%-40%, with the rest used for capex and debt reduction. Management expects debt to fall.

qa_highlights.question: Why did GCM margin fall from about 12% in Q1 to 10% in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Attributed to product mix, seasonality, and expedited freight and inbound/outbound material costs from supply chain constraints. Management said it is not a trend and the 10%-12% guidance is intact.

qa_highlights.question: Was there order bunching in GCM exports in Q2 given freight issues?
qa_highlights.answer: Possibly some customer pull-forward as a defensive measure. H2 growth may be below 22%-24% but still strong double-digit based on customer SAP commitments.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ICM aftermarket and OE spares growth, and when will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: OEM direct sales (about 50%-55% of ICM) grew 20%+; OE spares plus own aftermarket (about 45%) grew in single digits. Aftermarket dips when OEM demand booms.

qa_highlights.question: Is PLE's 14.4% margin sustainable and why did other income fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 14.4% is not sustainable on its own; Q1 and Q2 should be read together and the business is sustainable at double digits. Other income fell because last year's forex gains did not recur.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the H1 effective tax rate about 34.5% vs 27%-28% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly deferred tax, linked to significant deferred tax assets in overseas entities; expected to normalise as overseas operations streamline.

risks_watch: Europe demand weakness and volume reductions on awarded programmes; Germany flagged as weak.
SED margin recovery depends on agreeing new pricing with customers amid electronic component inflation and imported content.
Commodity prices, Middle East conflict and freight/shipping costs could affect H2 margins.
Standalone EBITDA grew only 3% in H1 while consolidated grew 40%; watch the standalone trajectory.
Effective tax rate running well above guidance; resolution depends on overseas streamlining.
Timing of STC hydraulic brake and actuator product launches, which management says could take 2-5 years to reach traction.
Halogen supplier insolvency and Trifa softness at PLE; ramp-up with largest US retailer must sustain.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the overall growth and margin recovery, especially GCM and ICM, but cautious on Europe, the H2 base effect, commodities and SED pricing. Several answers were evasive or deferred: brake segment size, tax payments, FY28 capex and the valuation question were not quantified.
key_quotes: I think we had talked about it earlier, and we expect some amount of bettering these numbers in Q3 too.
I would say that the restructuring at GCM is behind us, and I would say that is primarily the story behind these numbers.
I'm expecting that H2 may be slightly better than H1 in terms of margins.
It is not a pass-through, because we are not a process industry where we are only using steel, when there is a variation, it is very clear.

SED larger facility in vacated part of existing plant (construction started)
New STC building (Suprajit Technology Centre) due for completion in Q3 FY27

growth.why: Consolidated FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 12%-13.5% held with H2 margin guided slightly above H1; GCM strong double-digit H2 growth backed by customer commitments, and capex of ~INR200 crore reaffirmed, but no quantified revenue growth guide and SED/Europe pressures noted.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated H1 margin 12.1% with H2 guided slightly above H1 in percentage terms; GCM margin rose from 7.4% to 10%+ and ICM recovered to 15.3% from 12.8%, though SED margin is below double digits and commodity/Middle East risks remain.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: STC building due for completion in Q3 FY27, SED larger facility under construction and China plants have 8-9 of ~20-22 EV OEM projects in production with 10-12 more over the next year; no quantified capacity or utilisation figure was given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Consolidated revenue grew 22% in H1 to INR2,205 crore, GCM H2 guided to strong double-digit growth on customer commitments (H1 rate 22%-24%), though Europe volumes were cut (e.g. 500,000 to 300,000-400,000 sets on some programmes).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex is about INR200 crore with roughly half spent by mid-November and ongoing capex guided at 3%-4% of revenue; utilisation was not disclosed, and FY28 capex was not quantified on the call.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 consolidated margin guide of 12%-13.5% was held rather than raised, with H1 at 12.1%, and management flagged H2 base effects, commodities and Middle East conflict as headwinds.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 margin is conditional on commodity prices and the Middle East conflict, SED margins are under pressure from component inflation and pricing talks taking longer, and the H2 Indian auto base is higher.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: CBS brake production is ramping, a first drum brake system is going into production for an EV two-wheeler in Bengaluru, and first export parking brake supply has started; hydraulic brake positive news is expected next year, though management says traction may take 2-5 years.

rows.label: SED pricing renegotiation restores double-digit margin
rows.why: Management expects SED margins to return to double digits once new pricing is agreed, but SED Q2 electronics margin was below 10% and pricing talks are taking longer than expected.

rows.label: Net debt reduction and lower payouts
rows.why: Net debt fell to INR371 crore at 30 Sep 2026; payout guided at 30%-40% with the balance going to capex and debt reduction, and management expects debt to fall.

rows.label: Standalone EBITDA recovery
rows.why: Standalone H1 EBITDA grew only 3% to INR149 crore on 18% revenue growth, while consolidated EBITDA grew 40%, so standalone margin recovery is not yet visible.

tone.note: Management was confident on GCM and ICM margin recovery and on holding the 12%-13.5% FY27 margin guide, but cautious on Europe, the H2 base effect, commodities and SED pricing; analysts pushed on tax, brake segment size, FY28 capex and valuation, which were left unquantified.
